w3wp.exe spawning interpreter or LOLBin (http.sys exploitation / IIS RCE marker) AIExploitation High
CVE-2026-47291 is an integer overflow RCE in the Windows HTTP Protocol Stack (http.sys) — Microsoft flagged it as 'more likely' to be exploited and the article states 'an unauthenticated attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a specially crafted packet to a targeted server utilizing the HTTP Protocol Stack (http.sys) to process packets.' Since http.sys is the kernel front-end for IIS, successful exploitation typically results in code execution within w3wp.exe (the IIS worker process). Detects w3wp.exe spawning interpreters / LOLBins — the canonical web-shell / RCE post-condition. Rationale: Article quote: 'sending a specially crafted packet to a targeted server utilizing the HTTP Protocol Stack (http.sys) to process packets.' http.sys is the kernel-mode HTTP listener for IIS; successful code execution surfaces as w3wp.exe (the IIS application-pool worker) spawning interpreters or AD-discovery binaries. This pivot also catches the broader 'web-shell on IIS' family the same exploit chains into. Article-specific because the named component (http.sys) directly maps to w3wp.exe as the user-mode exploitation container.
ATT&CKT1190 T1505.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • SharePoint farm workflow services that shell out to PowerShell legitimately under specific app pools
  • Telligent / Sitecore extensibility that invokes cmd.exe for image processing
  • Custom in-house ASP.NET apps doing build/deploy hooks via Process.Start
  • Monitoring agents (SCOM, Datadog) deployed inside the app pool that call net.exe for service checks
  • Exchange On-Premises servers where w3wp.exe child processes are part of normal mailbox-tier behaviour
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !contains "SharePoint" and AccountName !in~ ("iis_iusrs","defaultapppool") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !contains "Microsoft\\Exchange Server"
Response runbook
Triage: Pull recent W3CIISLog / IIS access logs for the affected host and look for the request immediately preceding the child spawn — preserve raw URI + UserAgent + ClientIP for IR. Check whether http.sys / IIS KB for CVE-2026-47291 is installed. Contain: Stop the affected IIS app pool, isolate the host, preserve the inetpub folder for web-shell analysis, block the source IP at perimeter. Hunt: Search DeviceFileEvents for newly-written .aspx / .ashx / .asmx / .dll under inetpub paths in the prior 24h on the affected host (web-shell drops); pivot the source IP across other IIS servers in the fleet.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "w3wp.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","cscript.exe","wscript.exe","whoami.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","nltest.exe","ipconfig.exe","systeminfo.exe","netstat.exe","tasklist.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          AppPoolCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith @"\w3wp.exe"
| where NewProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","cscript.exe","wscript.exe","whoami.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","nltest.exe","ipconfig.exe","systeminfo.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account = SubjectUserName,
          AppPoolCmd = ParentProcessName,
          ChildImage = NewProcessName,
          ChildCmd = CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Hyper-V worker process (vmwp.exe / vmms.exe) spawning unexpected child (guest-to-host escape) AIExploitation Medium
Targets CVE-2026-45607, CVE-2026-45641 and CVE-2026-47652 — out-of-bounds reads in Hyper-V where, per the article, 'an authenticated attacker on a guest virtual machine (VM) sends specially crafted file operation requests to hardware resources within the VM which could result in remote code execution on the host server.' Successful exploitation surfaces as code running in the host-side vmwp.exe (per-VM worker) or vmms.exe (VMMS) — both of which have an empty baseline for child-process spawning. Rationale: Article quote: 'an authenticated attacker on a guest virtual machine (VM) sends specially crafted file operation requests to hardware resources within the VM which could result in remote code execution on the host server.' Host-side vmwp.exe is the per-VM worker that handles guest hardware emulation — RCE in this process is the canonical guest-to-host escape primitive. Both vmwp.exe and vmms.exe have a near-empty child-process baseline on production Hyper-V hosts, giving very high signal-to-noise.
ATT&CKT1068 T1611
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • SCVMM / VMM agent deployments that shell helpers from vmms during checkpoint operations
  • Hyper-V Live Migration triggering transient helper processes during cluster failover
  • Veeam / Commvault Hyper-V backup integration spawning helper binaries under vmms context
  • Customer-written PowerShell Direct sessions that pivot through vmwp for guest management
  • Microsoft cluster validation wizard producing diagnostic child processes
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !contains "Virtual Machine Manager" and FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files\Veeam\" and FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files\Commvault\"
Response runbook
Triage: Identify the GUID of the VM whose vmwp.exe spawned the child (the command line of vmwp contains a -GuestType + VM GUID) — that is the candidate compromised guest. Verify whether CVE-2026-45607 / CVE-2026-45641 / CVE-2026-47652 KBs are deployed to the host. Contain: Pause the suspect guest VM (do NOT shut down — preserve memory state for forensics), isolate the Hyper-V host from the management network, snapshot guest memory via vm2dmp / live snapshot. Hunt: Search DeviceFileEvents on the host for unusual writes to %ProgramData%\Microsoft\Windows\Hyper-V\ in the last 24h; pivot on the suspect guest's vNIC MAC to find anomalous east-west traffic. Restore guest from a pre-incident checkpoint after host KB applied.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("vmwp.exe","vmms.exe","vmcompute.exe")
| where FileName !in~ ("WerFault.exe","WerFaultSecure.exe","conhost.exe","vmcompute.exe","vmwp.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          HyperVParent = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          ChildIntegrity = ProcessIntegrityLevel,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith @"\vmwp.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith @"\vmms.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith @"\vmcompute.exe"
| where NewProcessName !endswith @"\conhost.exe"
   and NewProcessName !endswith @"\WerFault.exe"
   and NewProcessName !endswith @"\WerFaultSecure.exe"
   and NewProcessName !endswith @"\vmcompute.exe"
   and NewProcessName !endswith @"\vmwp.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account = SubjectUserName,
          HyperVParent = ParentProcessName,
          ChildImage = NewProcessName,
          ChildCmd = CommandLine,
          TokenElevationType
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Python interpreter downloads oven-sh Bun runtime v1.3.14 from GitHub releases at import time AIInstallation High
Hunts for the Hades Campaign entry hook embedded in compromised PyPI packages (ensmallen, embiggen, gpsea, pyphetools, etc.). The deobfuscated import hook in __init__.py downloads bun-{linux,darwin,windows}-{x64,aarch64}.zip from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.14/. A Python package fetching a Bun runtime at import is not legitimate behaviour. Rationale: Anchors on the exact URL prefix github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.14/ and the four ZIP filename variants enumerated in the deobfuscated hook. A Python interpreter pulling a Bun runtime at import is highly anomalous — Bun is a Node.js alternative, not a Python dependency.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1105 T1059.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer manually scripting a Bun install from a Python helper (`subprocess.run(['python','install_bun.py'])`)
  • Polyglot test/CI tooling that legitimately bootstraps Bun in Python build steps
  • Security researcher reproducing the Hades sample in a sandbox
  • Educational notebooks demonstrating multi-runtime tooling
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("install_bun.py","setup_bun.py","build/bootstrap") and AccountName endswith "-build")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Identify the parent Python invocation — capture ProcessCommandLine and the site-packages folder. Cross-check against the affected PyPI package list (ensmallen 0.8.101, mflux-streamlit 0.0.3/0.0.4, nhmpy 2.4.7, ppkt2synergy 0.1.1, embiggen 0.11.97, gpsea 0.9.14, pyphetools 0.9.120). Step 2 (contain): Isolate the host, kill any running `bun` process, remove `/tmp/.bun_ran` and the `bun` binary from `/tmp/b/` (or %TEMP%\b\), uninstall the offending package with `pip uninstall --yes <pkg>`. Rotate any developer secrets exposed via env vars on the host. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot DeviceProcessEvents for the same SHA256 of the dropped bun binary across the fleet, search EmailEvents/audit logs for the install command, check GitHub Actions runner inventory for Runner.Worker exposure.
let Lookback = 14d;
// Hades Campaign import hook fetches a Bun runtime zip from oven-sh/bun releases
let NetSide = DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(Lookback)
  | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","python","python3","pythonw.exe")
  | where RemoteUrl has "oven-sh/bun/releases/download" or RemoteUrl has "github.com/oven-sh/bun"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, ReportId, DeviceId;
let FileSide = DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(Lookback)
  | where ActionType == "FileCreated"
  | where FileName matches regex @"^bun-(linux|darwin|windows)-(x64|aarch64)\.zip$" or FileName =~ "b.zip"
  | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","python","python3")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ReportId, DeviceId;
NetSide | union FileSide
| order by Timestamp desc
let Lookback = 14d;
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("python.exe","python3.exe","python","python3")
| where Url has_any ("oven-sh/bun/releases/download","github.com/oven-sh/bun")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, Url, DstIpAddr, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| union (
    ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where EventType == "FileCreated"
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("python.exe","python3.exe","python","python3")
    | where TargetFileName matches regex @"^bun-(linux|darwin|windows)-(x64|aarch64)\.zip$" or TargetFileName =~ "b.zip"
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
  )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Bun runtime executed from temp directory by Python interpreter (Hades vF203 loader) AIInstallation High
Detects the Hades Campaign second-stage: the import hook executes the dropped Bun binary from /tmp/b/bun (or %TEMP%\b\bun) with `run _index.js`, where _index.js is located by crawling sys.path. The parent-Python → child-Bun-in-tempdir process tree is the campaign's defining behavioural signature. Rationale: Anchors on the exact loader chain shown in the deobfuscated hook: parent=python, child=bun, command-line contains `_index.js`, image path under the temp-`b` subdirectory the hook creates. Bun spawned by Python in a tempdir is unique to this campaign.
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1059.006 T1218
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Polyglot test runners that explicitly spawn Bun from Python wrapper scripts
  • Local developer experiments with Bun + Python interop
  • Security analyst detonating the sample in a sandbox VM
  • CI/CD scripts intentionally bootstrapping Bun via a Python helper (rare)
Suppression filter
| where not (AccountName endswith "-ci" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "polyglot_runner.py")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Capture the full process tree (python → bun → _index.js) plus the SHA256 of the bun binary and the resolved path to _index.js. Compare bun's SHA256 to the official oven-sh/bun v1.3.14 release hash — a match still indicates compromise since the loader is legitimate Bun running attacker JS. Step 2 (contain): Kill the bun process, delete the `b/` temp directory, remove `/tmp/.bun_ran` flag file, isolate the host. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot DeviceNetworkEvents from this DeviceId in the next 1h window for outbound C2 (campaign deploys cross-platform memory scrapers + GitHub-based exfil); check for Runner.Worker process memory access; review which PyPI package's __init__.py was the entry — the site-packages parent of `_index.js` identifies the compromised package.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","python","python3","pythonw.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("bun","bun.exe")
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Temp\b\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\b\", "/tmp/b/", "/var/folders/")
   or ProcessCommandLine has "_index.js"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("python.exe","python3.exe","python","python3","pythonw.exe")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("bun","bun.exe")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has "_index.js"
   or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (@"\Temp\b\", "/tmp/b/", "/var/folders/")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, SHA256

Cross-platform memory scraping of GitHub Actions Runner.Worker process AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts the Hades Campaign credential-exfil stage. On Linux runners the malware reads /proc/{pid}/maps and /proc/{pid}/mem of the Runner.Worker process; on macOS it uses ctypes-loaded libc with task_for_pid + vm_region_basic_info_64. Either signal on a GitHub Actions runner host is high-fidelity credential theft. Rationale: Anchors on the article's exact memory-scrape primitives: /proc/{pid}/mem and /proc/{pid}/maps for Linux, and the ctypes Mach APIs (task_for_pid, vm_region_basic_info_64, mach_task_self_) for macOS — plus the specific target process name `Runner.Worker`. These appear nowhere in benign development workflows.
ATT&CKT1003 T1057 T1552.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate observability tools (py-spy, gdb attach, perf script) reading /proc/<pid>/mem on dev workstations
  • Memory profiling of self-hosted runner debug sessions
  • macOS Activity Monitor / Instruments probing process VM regions
  • Security tooling (e.g. Lacework, Sysdig) sampling process memory for inventory
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("py-spy","gdb","perf","lacework_agent") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("py-spy dump","py-spy record","gdb -p"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Confirm the host is a GitHub Actions self-hosted runner (check for ~/_work/, actions-runner/ directory, Runner.Listener process). Pull the full /proc reader's parent chain — should resolve to a python or bun process from a recently-installed PyPI package. Step 2 (contain): Stop the runner service (`./svc.sh stop`), revoke the runner registration token, rotate ALL secrets the runner has access to (repository secrets, environment secrets, OIDC tokens, cloud credentials assumed by jobs in the past 14 days). Treat every secret accessible to that runner as compromised. Step 3 (hunt): Pull GitHub audit log for workflow runs on that runner since the suspected install; review outbound network from runner to api.github.com (the campaign exfils via GitHub); search organization repos for new private repos named like `Shai-Hulud` or unexpected commits authored by tokens issued to the runner.
// Hades Campaign Runner.Worker memory scrape — Linux /proc reads and macOS Mach VM APIs
let LinuxScrape = DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
  | where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"/proc/\d+/(mem|maps)"
  | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3","bun")
     or FileName in~ ("python","python3","bun","cat","dd","strings");
let MacScrape = DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
  | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3")
  | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("task_for_pid","vm_region_basic_info_64","mach_task_self_","vm_read_overwrite")
     or ProcessCommandLine has "Runner.Worker";
let RunnerContext = DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
  | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3","bun") or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("Runner.Listener","Runner.Worker")
  | where ProcessCommandLine has "Runner.Worker";
LinuxScrape | union MacScrape | union RunnerContext
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let Lookback = 14d;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where (ParentProcessName has_any ("python","python3","bun"))
   and (TargetProcessCommandLine matches regex @"/proc/\d+/(mem|maps)"
        or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("task_for_pid","vm_region_basic_info_64","mach_task_self_","Runner.Worker"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| union (
    Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where Facility == "authpriv" or ProcessName == "audit"
    | where SyslogMessage matches regex @"/proc/\d+/(mem|maps)" and (SyslogMessage has "python" or SyslogMessage has "bun")
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname=Computer, ActorUsername="", TargetProcessName=ProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine=SyslogMessage, ParentProcessName="", ParentProcessCommandLine=""
  )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

(#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 OR #event_simpleName=SyntheticProcessRollup2)
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(python3?|bun)$/i OR ImageFileName=/[\\\/](python3?|bun)$/i
| regex("(/proc/[0-9]+/(mem|maps)|task_for_pid|vm_region_basic_info_64|mach_task_self_|Runner\\.Worker)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

Malicious _hooks.py / _runtime.bin files created in Pythagora gpt-pilot checkout AIDelivery High
Detects the on-endpoint outcome of the GitHub force-push attack documented in the article timeline: the malicious commit (065ee8eb) by the compromised LeonOstrez account introduced _hooks.py, _runtime.bin, and modified __init__.py. Any developer who pulled main between 11:13 and ~12:00 UTC on 2026-06-08 received these files on disk. Rationale: Article Table 2 names the malicious commit 065ee8eb as adding exactly _hooks.py and _runtime.bin plus modifying __init__.py. Pairing these filenames with a git/IDE writer captures the moment the malicious commit lands on a developer machine — before any execution happens.
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1554
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal repos with their own benign _hooks.py file unrelated to gpt-pilot
  • Developer creating a placeholder _runtime.bin for an unrelated project
  • IDE template scaffolding that generates similarly-named files
  • Pre-2026-06-08 cached copies in old checkouts being re-extracted
Suppression filter
| where not (FolderPath has_any ("\\node_modules\\","\\.venv\\","\\site-packages\\") and not (FolderPath has_any ("gpt-pilot","pythagora")))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Resolve the FolderPath to determine which git repo the files landed in — confirm it's a clone of github.com/Pythagora-io/gpt-pilot. Run `git log --all _hooks.py _runtime.bin` in the checkout to extract the commit SHA (expect 065ee8eb if compromised pre-revert). Step 2 (contain): Delete the working checkout, force users off the compromised branch, advise `git fetch && git reset --hard origin/main` only AFTER confirming origin/main has been reverted by the maintainers. Block the LeonOstrez user/PAT at the GitHub org level. Step 3 (hunt): For every host that received these files, pivot to UC1/UC2 detections — did the developer ever run `python` or open the project in an IDE after the pull? If yes, treat as a UC2/UC3 incident and rotate credentials accessible from that workstation.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where FileName in~ ("_hooks.py","_runtime.bin")
   or (FileName =~ "__init__.py" and FolderPath has_any ("gpt-pilot","pythagora"))
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("git.exe","git","gh.exe","gh","Code.exe","cursor.exe","pycharm64.exe","PyCharm","idea64.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName has_any ("git.exe","git","gh.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("_hooks.py","_runtime.bin")
   or (TargetFileName =~ "__init__.py" and TargetFilePath has_any ("gpt-pilot","pythagora"))
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("git.exe","git","gh.exe","gh","Code.exe","cursor.exe","pycharm64.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine

pip / uv install of known-compromised Hades Campaign PyPI package versions AIDelivery High
Alerts on installation of any PyPI package version explicitly named in the Hades Campaign affected-versions table. Catches both pre-detection installs (already on disk) and ongoing installs from CI pipelines that pin to vulnerable versions. Rationale: Anchored to the exact (package, version) pairs in the article's Affected Versions table. Version-pinned matches give near-zero false positive rate — the only way to hit is to install the named version. File-side fallback catches lockfile installs that don't appear in process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher / IR detonating the sample in a sandbox
  • Internal copies of the package mirror cached pre-compromise (versions match but artifacts are clean)
  • Reproducibility build of an old project still pinning the vulnerable version after maintainers re-release a clean version under the same number
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("malware-sandbox","ir-detonation","securitylab") or AccountName in~ ("malware-analyst","ir-detonator"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Identify the host and user that ran the install — pull the full pip command line, requirements.txt / pyproject.toml path, and any CI job ID. Confirm site-packages contains the package by reading FolderPath. Step 2 (contain): `pip uninstall --yes <pkg>` on the host, delete cached wheels from ~/.cache/pip/wheels/, remove the package from any requirements files and rebuild lockfiles. If the host is a CI runner, stop the runner and rotate its secrets per UC3 runbook. Step 3 (hunt): Cross-reference with UC1 (Bun download) and UC2 (Bun execution) on the same DeviceId in the +24h window — if either fires, escalate. Search internal package mirrors / Artifactory caches for the affected versions and quarantine them. Notify affected developers to rotate any tokens that lived in their environment.
let Pkgs = dynamic(["ensmallen==0.8.101","ensmallen 0.8.101","mflux-streamlit==0.0.3","mflux-streamlit==0.0.4","nhmpy==2.4.7","ppkt2synergy==0.1.1","embiggen==0.11.97","gpsea==0.9.14","pyphetools==0.9.120"]);
let ProcSide = DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where FileName in~ ("pip.exe","pip","pip3.exe","pip3","uv.exe","uv","poetry.exe","poetry")
     or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("pip","pip3","pip.exe","pip3.exe","uv","poetry")
  | where ProcessCommandLine has_any (Pkgs)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath;
let FileSide = DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where ActionType == "FileCreated"
  | where FolderPath has "site-packages"
  | where FolderPath matches regex @"(?i)site-packages[\\/](ensmallen|mflux[_-]streamlit|nhmpy|ppkt2synergy|embiggen|gpsea|pyphetools)([\\/-]|$)"
  | where FileName endswith ".py" or FileName endswith "METADATA" or FileName endswith "RECORD"
  | summarize FilesDropped=count(), AnyFile=any(FolderPath), FirstSeen=min(Timestamp) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
  | project Timestamp=FirstSeen, DeviceName, AccountName="(from-installer)", ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath=AnyFile;
ProcSide | union FileSide
| order by Timestamp desc
let Pkgs = dynamic(["ensmallen==0.8.101","mflux-streamlit==0.0.3","mflux-streamlit==0.0.4","nhmpy==2.4.7","ppkt2synergy==0.1.1","embiggen==0.11.97","gpsea==0.9.14","pyphetools==0.9.120"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("pip","pip3","uv","poetry")
   or ParentProcessName has_any ("pip","pip3","uv","poetry")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (Pkgs)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName
| union (
    ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where EventType == "FileCreated"
    | where TargetFilePath has "site-packages"
    | where TargetFilePath matches regex @"(?i)site-packages[\\/](ensmallen|mflux[_-]streamlit|nhmpy|ppkt2synergy|embiggen|gpsea|pyphetools)([\\/-]|$)"
    | summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), Path=any(TargetFilePath) by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName
    | project TimeGenerated=FirstSeen, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName=ActingProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine=Path, ParentProcessName=""
  )
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Hades Campaign Compromised PyPI Package Install
id: 4d92c8e1-7b34-4d6f-913c-6a8e2f1d05a4
description: Detects pip / uv / poetry installation of any PyPI package version listed in the Hades Campaign affected-versions table (ensmallen 0.8.101, embiggen 0.11.97, etc.).
references:

author: SOC Detection Engineering

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Miasma Worm Hits Microsoft Again: Azure Functions Action and 72 Other Repositories Disabled After Supply Chain Attack Targeting AI Coding Agents

StepSecurity
2026-06-09 12 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

On June 5, 2026, the Miasma worm campaign reached Microsoft's Azure GitHub organizations. GitHub disabled 73 repositories across four Microsoft GitHub organizations after a malicious commit was pushed to the Azure/durabletask repository using a previously compromised contributor account. The attack planted configuration files that execute a credential-harvesting payload when a developer opens the repository in Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor, or VS Code.

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Suspicious commit pattern: '[skip ci]' with backdated timestamp adding only IDE config files · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] node.exe spawned by Code/Cursor/Claude/Gemini executing .github/setup.js · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Miasma Worm Hits Microsoft Again: Azure Functions Action and 72 Other Repositori
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Malicious AI coding-agent hook configs written to repo (.claude/.gemini/.cursor/.vscode)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound DNS / HTTP to Miasma C2 (git-service.com / m-kosche.com) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Malicious AI coding-agent hook configs written to repo (.claude/.gemini/.cursor/.vscode) AIInstallation High
Hunts the Miasma worm's signature artifact: simultaneous creation of SessionStart hooks and folderOpen tasks in .claude/settings.json, .gemini/settings.json, .cursor/rules/setup.mdc, and .vscode/tasks.json — all pointing at node .github/setup.js. This is the precise file-set planted in the June 5 2026 Azure/durabletask commit 5f456b8. Rationale: The five planted-file paths are verbatim from the article's 'Five Planted Files, Four Attack Vectors' section. Requiring >=2 co-occurrence per host suppresses single legitimate .vscode/tasks.json edits while keeping near-zero FP on the Miasma file-set. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/ • https://github.com/step-security/supply-chain-firewall
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer scaffolding a new repo with VS Code tasks.json AND committing a .vscode workspace file at the same time
  • Engineering platform team rolling out a corporate .cursor/rules/ template across repos
  • Repo containing legitimate .github/setup.js for project bootstrapping (rare; size + obfuscation differentiates)
  • Renovate/Dependabot edits to .vscode/tasks.json without other paired files (will not trigger >=2 threshold)
  • Developer copying a template repo locally that legitimately includes both .claude and .vscode dirs
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("git.exe","Code.exe","Cursor.exe") and array_length(ArtifactsSeen) == 1 and ArtifactsSeen has "vscode-folderopen")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull the InitiatingProcess (typically git.exe / Code.exe checkout) and inspect the .github/setup.js size and entropy; the Miasma payload is exactly 4,643,745 bytes single-line obfuscated JS. Pivot to DeviceProcessEvents for any node.exe child within 60s. Step 2 — Contain: isolate the host, kill any node setup.js process tree, force-revoke the developer's GitHub PAT / OAuth tokens, cloud CLI tokens (aws, az, gcloud), and rotate any .npmrc / .pypirc / kubeconfig secrets that the harvester targets. Step 3 — Hunt: search the org for any repo containing the five planted paths via GitHub code-search API; check for outbound DNS to check.git-service.com / t.m-kosche.com / git-service.com from any developer endpoint in the past 30 days.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\.claude\settings.json", @"\.gemini\settings.json", @"\.cursor\rules\setup.mdc", @"\.vscode\tasks.json", @"\.github\setup.js")
| extend Artifact = case(
    FolderPath has @"\.claude\settings.json", "claude-hook",
    FolderPath has @"\.gemini\settings.json", "gemini-hook",
    FolderPath has @"\.cursor\rules\setup.mdc", "cursor-prompt-injection",
    FolderPath has @"\.vscode\tasks.json", "vscode-folderopen",
    FolderPath has @"\.github\setup.js", "miasma-payload", "other")
| summarize ArtifactsSeen = make_set(Artifact), Paths = make_set(FolderPath), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp) by DeviceId, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| where array_length(ArtifactsSeen) >= 2  // co-occurrence of >=2 of the 5 planted files
| order by FirstSeen desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileCreate")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\.claude\settings.json", @"\.gemini\settings.json", @"\.cursor\rules\setup.mdc", @"\.vscode\tasks.json", @"\.github\setup.js")
| extend Artifact = case(
    TargetFilePath has @"\.claude\settings.json", "claude-hook",
    TargetFilePath has @"\.gemini\settings.json", "gemini-hook",
    TargetFilePath has @"\.cursor\rules\setup.mdc", "cursor-prompt-injection",
    TargetFilePath has @"\.vscode\tasks.json", "vscode-folderopen",
    TargetFilePath has @"\.github\setup.js", "miasma-payload", "other")
| summarize ArtifactsSeen = make_set(Artifact), Paths = make_set(TargetFilePath), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated) by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName
| where array_length(ArtifactsSeen) >= 2
| order by FirstSeen desc
title: Miasma Worm AI-Agent Hook Config Planted
id: 8a2a4e0f-3d9c-4b7d-9b4f-1d2e7c61a210
description: Detects creation of SessionStart hooks / folderOpen tasks / Cursor prompt-injection rules that the Miasma worm plants in compromised repos to auto-execute node .github/setup.js when a developer opens the project in Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor, or VS Code.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/miasma-worm-hits-microsoft-again-azure-functions-action-and-72-other-repositories-disabled-after-supply-chain-attack-targeting-ai-coding-agents
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/06
tags:
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1546
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '\.claude\settings.json'
      - '\.gemini\settings.json'
      - '\.cursor\rules\setup.mdc'
      - '\.vscode\tasks.json'
      - '\.github\setup.js'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 (@TargetFilename:(*\\.claude\\settings.json OR *\\.gemini\\settings.json OR *\\.cursor\\rules\\setup.mdc OR *\\.vscode\\tasks.json OR *\\.github\\setup.js))
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| TargetFileName=/\\\.(claude|gemini)\\\\settings\.json$|\\\.cursor\\\\rules\\\\setup\.mdc$|\\\.vscode\\\\tasks\.json$|\\\.github\\\\setup\.js$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName], function=[count(), collect(TargetFileName)])
| _count >= 2
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*\\.claude\\settings.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.gemini\\settings.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.cursor\\rules\\setup.mdc" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.vscode\\tasks.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.github\\setup.js") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where mvcount(paths)>=2
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*\\.claude\\settings.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.gemini\\settings.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.cursor\\rules\\setup.mdc" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.vscode\\tasks.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.github\\setup.js") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where mvcount(paths)>=2
node.exe spawned by Code/Cursor/Claude/Gemini executing .github/setup.js AIExploitation High
Hunts the Miasma worm's automatic execution chain: VS Code, Cursor, Claude Code, or Gemini CLI launching node.exe with .github/setup.js as the script argument. This is the runtime detonation produced when a developer simply opens a repo containing the planted hook configs. Rationale: Article quotes the exact command 'node .github/setup.js' invoked by all four planted configs (Claude SessionStart, Gemini SessionStart, Cursor prompt injection, VS Code folderOpen task). Anchoring on parent IDE + node.exe + setup.js path is high-fidelity because legitimate projects rarely store bootstrap scripts under .github/. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1546/ • https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/editor/tasks#_run-behavior
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1546 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer with a legitimate project-bootstrap node script genuinely under .github/setup.js
  • Internal devtools team running .github/setup.js via VS Code task as a sanctioned scaffold
  • CI runner image with cached IDE binaries executing setup scripts during build
  • Repo template repos where setup.js is an intentional installer
  • Security researcher analysing the Miasma sample in a sandbox (whitelist sandbox host IDs)
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has "sandbox" or DeviceName has "malware-lab")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: hash the setup.js (expect 4,643,745 bytes / SHA256 mismatch to any known-good repo) and capture the first 1 KB of the single-line obfuscated JS for IR. Pull network egress from the node.exe PID. Step 2 — Contain: kill the node process tree, isolate the host, and revoke developer-context credentials — GitHub PAT/OAuth, AWS/Azure/GCP CLI tokens, kubeconfig, NPM/PyPI tokens, SSH keys (article confirms harvester targets AWS/Azure/GCP/Kubernetes + 90+ dev tool configs). Step 3 — Hunt: enumerate all repos cloned on the host in the past 30 days and check each working tree for the five planted paths; sweep the org's GitHub for commits with message 'Switched DataConverter to OrchestrationContext [skip ci]' or backdated commits to 2020-03-09.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "node.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (@".github\setup.js", ".github/setup.js")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("Code.exe","Cursor.exe","claude.exe","claude-code.exe","gemini.exe","node.exe","powershell.exe","cmd.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "node.exe"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (@".github\setup.js", ".github/setup.js")
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("Code.exe","Cursor.exe","claude.exe","claude-code.exe","gemini.exe","node.exe","powershell.exe","cmd.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Miasma Worm node.exe Auto-Executing .github/setup.js From IDE

description: Detects node.exe spawned by VS Code, Cursor, Claude Code, or Gemini CLI with .github/setup.js on the command line — the Miasma worm's auto-execution on folder open.

author: SOC Detection Engineering

logsource:

#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2

ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name=node.exe (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("Code.exe","Cursor.exe","claude.exe","claude-code.exe","gemini.exe","node.exe")) (Processes.process="*.github\\setup.js*" OR Processes.process="*.github/setup.js*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name=node.exe (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("Code.exe","Cursor.exe","claude.exe","claude-code.exe","gemini.exe","node.exe")) (Processes.process="*.github\\setup.js*" OR Processes.process="*.github/setup.js*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Outbound DNS / HTTP to Miasma C2 (git-service.com / m-kosche.com) AICommand & Control High
Hunts resolution or connection to the Miasma worm's credential-exfiltration infrastructure: check.git-service.com, git-service.com, and t.m-kosche.com. These domains receive harvested AWS/Azure/GCP/Kubernetes/dev-tool secrets from the planted payload. Rationale: Three domains are explicitly listed in the article's pre-extracted IOCs (check.git-service.com, t.m-kosche.com, git-service.com). Article says credential-harvesting payload exfiltrates AWS/Azure/GCP/Kubernetes/dev-tool secrets, so DNS+network egress to these domains is high-fidelity C2. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/miasma-worm-hits-microsoft-again-azure-functions-action-and-72-other-repositories-disabled-after-supply-chain-attack-targeting-ai-coding-agents
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041 T1568
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate enterprise self-hosted Git on a sub-domain that coincidentally matches *git-service.com (rare; whitelist by exact FQDN)
  • Threat-intel feed fetcher / sandbox detonation system (whitelist sandbox host IDs)
  • Security researcher visiting the domain for reverse-engineering
  • DNS sinkhole or RPZ infrastructure resolving the indicator (whitelist sinkhole resolver IP)
  • Browsing to the StepSecurity blog post itself (won't hit subdomains directly)
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("sinkhole","sandbox","ti-fetcher"))
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: identify the initiating process and user; if InitiatingProcessFileName is node.exe, immediately pivot to its command line for .github/setup.js. Step 2 — Contain: isolate the host, block the three domains at the corporate resolver and egress proxy, and treat all credentials accessible from the user/host context as compromised — rotate cloud tokens, GitHub PATs, NPM/PyPI/Cargo registry tokens, kubeconfig, SSH keys. Step 3 — Hunt: 30-day lookback across the entire fleet for any resolution of git-service.com or m-kosche.com; correlate hits with file-creation of .github/setup.js or the four IDE hook configs to find latent infections.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("git-service.com","m-kosche.com") or RemoteUrl in~ ("check.git-service.com","t.m-kosche.com","git-service.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (DnsEvents
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
   | where Name has_any ("git-service.com","m-kosche.com")
   | project TimeGenerated, Host = Computer, ClientIP, Domain = Name, QueryType = QueryTypeName, Result),
  (ImDnsActivity
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
   | where DnsQuery has_any ("git-service.com","m-kosche.com")
   | project TimeGenerated, Host = SrcHostname, ClientIP = SrcIpAddr, Domain = DnsQuery, QueryType = DnsQueryTypeName, Result = DnsResponseCodeName),
  (CommonSecurityLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
   | where DestinationDnsDomain has_any ("git-service.com","m-kosche.com") or RequestURL has_any ("git-service.com","m-kosche.com")
   | project TimeGenerated, Host = SourceHostName, ClientIP = SourceIP, Domain = coalesce(DestinationDnsDomain, RequestURL), QueryType = "proxy", Result = DeviceAction)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Suspicious commit pattern: '[skip ci]' with backdated timestamp adding only IDE config files AIDelivery Medium
Hunts the Miasma commit fingerprint: a single push where 5 files added / 0 source files modified, commit message ends with '[skip ci]', author date backdated to a pre-2024 timestamp, and the added paths include AI-agent config dirs. Detects via GitHub Audit Log shipped to Sentinel/Defender via CloudAppEvents or to Datadog via the GitHub integration. Rationale: Article details the exact commit fingerprint: commit 5f456b8 with message 'Switched DataConverter to OrchestrationContext [skip ci]', 5 files added / 0 source files modified, backdated to 2020-03-09T15:59:47Z (six years before push). The conjunction of [skip ci] + backdated author date + added IDE-config paths is the Miasma operator signature. Cross-checked against: • https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/admin/monitoring-activity-in-your-enterprise/reviewing-audit-logs-for-your-enterprise
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1078.004
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate maintainer importing an old Git history with [skip ci] in a merge commit
  • Repository migration from another VCS preserving original author dates pre-2024
  • CI maintenance commit adding .vscode/tasks.json with [skip ci] (will not match >=2 of the IDE paths usually)
  • Bot commits (Renovate/Dependabot) with skip-ci that touch tasks.json
  • Developer rebasing old branches with preserved author timestamps
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull the actor account from the audit event, check its recent activity for token regeneration / SSH key additions / new OAuth grants; correlate against the May 19 PyPI durabletask incident actor. Step 2 — Contain: suspend the GitHub account, revoke all PATs and OAuth grants, force-rotate any GitHub App / Action secrets the account had access to, and revert the commit from any affected default branches. Step 3 — Hunt: GitHub code-search the org for any other repos containing the five planted paths or the commit message 'Switched DataConverter to OrchestrationContext'; query GitHub Audit Log for the same actor across all owned orgs for [skip ci] commits adding files outside src trees.
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where Application == "GitHub"
| where ActionType in ("Repositories.Push","RepositoriesPush","git.push")
| extend Raw = tostring(RawEventData)
| where Raw has "[skip ci]"
| where Raw has_any (".claude/settings.json",".gemini/settings.json",".cursor/rules/setup.mdc",".vscode/tasks.json",".github/setup.js")
| extend AuthorDate = extract(@"author[^\d]+(\d{4})-\d{2}-\d{2}", 1, Raw)
| where isnotempty(AuthorDate) and toint(AuthorDate) < 2024
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, IPAddress, ObjectName, AuthorDate, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
// Requires GitHub Audit Log connector (GitHubAuditLogPolling_CL) or CommonSecurityLog ingest
GitHubAuditLogPolling_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where action_s == "git.push" or action_s == "repo.push"
| where commits_s has "[skip ci]"
| where commits_s has_any (".claude/settings.json",".gemini/settings.json",".cursor/rules/setup.mdc",".vscode/tasks.json",".github/setup.js")
| extend AuthorYear = extract(@"author[^\d]+(\d{4})-\d{2}-\d{2}", 1, commits_s)
| where isnotempty(AuthorYear) and toint(AuthorYear) < 2024
| project TimeGenerated, actor_s, actor_ip_s, repo_s, commits_s, AuthorYear
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:github @evt.name:git.push @commits.message:*"[skip ci]"* (@commits.added:(*.claude/settings.json* OR *.gemini/settings.json* OR *.cursor/rules/setup.mdc* OR *.vscode/tasks.json* OR *.github/setup.js*))
CLOUD
`github_audit` action=git.push | spath input=raw_event | search commits{}.message="*[skip ci]*" (commits{}.added{}="*.claude/settings.json" OR commits{}.added{}="*.gemini/settings.json" OR commits{}.added{}="*.cursor/rules/setup.mdc" OR commits{}.added{}="*.vscode/tasks.json" OR commits{}.added{}="*.github/setup.js") | eval author_year=substr('commits{}.timestamp',1,4) | where author_year<"2024" | table _time repo actor commits{}.id commits{}.message commits{}.added{} author_year
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("") or RemoteUrl has_any ("check.git-service.com", "t.m-kosche.com", "git-service.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic([""]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["check.git-service.com", "t.m-kosche.com", "git-service.com"]);

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)

| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")

                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")

     | rename dest AS src]

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant

level: medium

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"

     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`

| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",

           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",

                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer

status: experimental
description: |

    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.

            - 'invoke-expression'

Miasma C2 / IOC domain resolution: check.git-service.com, t.m-kosche.com, git-service.com AICommand & Control High
Detects DNS resolution or HTTP egress to known Miasma/Shai-Hulud campaign C2 infrastructure embedded in trojanized PyPI packages and Microsoft GitHub repos. The domains are used both for stealer beaconing and exfil-target discovery. Rationale: Article + pre-extracted IOC bundle name the three exact campaign domains; Socket and StepSecurity write-ups on Shai-Hulud / Miasma corroborate git-service.com as campaign infrastructure. DNS-layer detection catches resolution even if HTTPS prevents URL inspection. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/ • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A legitimate internal service named 'git-service' resolving to a different parent domain — confirm by checking the full FQDN
  • Threat-intel feed validation traffic from a TIP / sandbox VM (will originate from analyst hosts)
  • Security researcher reproducing the campaign on a sandbox endpoint
  • Web crawler / vuln scanner crawling threat-intel articles that reference the domains as text
Suppression filter

Response runbook
1. Triage: Pivot on DeviceName + InitiatingProcessFileName — is the calling process python.exe / pip.exe / node.exe / bun.exe / an IDE process (code.exe, cursor.exe, pycharm64.exe)? If yes, treat as confirmed Miasma stage-2 beacon. 2. Contain: Isolate the device via Defender Live Response, kill the calling process, and quarantine any newly-created files in %APPDATA%, AppData\Local\Temp, and the user's Python site-packages. Block the three domains at egress proxy + DNS sinkhole. 3. Hunt: Pull all `pip install` / `uv add` / `poetry add` history for the user in the last 30 days, cross-check against the campaign package list, and search GitHub for any new public repos created by the developer's GH account in the same window (data-exfil destination per Socket).
